question_text: Identify the product which represents the solid state in the above reaction.
answer_text: Barium sulphate
answer_explanation: In the reaction between barium chloride and sodium sulphate, insoluble barium sulphate forms as a white precipitate.

question_text: The colour of the solution observed after 30 minutes of placing zinc metal to copper sulphate solution is
answer_text: Colourless
answer_explanation: Zinc displaces copper from copper sulphate, forming colourless zinc sulphate solution and reddish-brown copper.

question_text: Mild non-corrosive basic salt is
answer_text: NaHCO3
answer_explanation: Sodium hydrogen carbonate is a mild, non-corrosive basic salt.

question_text: On adding dilute s ulphuric acid to a test tube containing a metal ‘X’, a colourless gas is produced when a burning match stick is brought near it. Which of the following correctly represents metal ‘X’?
answer_text: Sodium
answer_explanation: Sodium reacts with dilute sulphuric acid to release hydrogen gas, which burns with a pop sound.

question_text: Which one of the following correctly represents Sodium oxide? (shown as electron-dot/Lewis structures of the ionic bonding between sodium and oxygen)
options: One Na ion with a +2 charge, and two oxide ions [O]2- each shown with 8 dots (4 lone pairs)
Two Na+ ions, and one oxide ion [O]2- shown with 8 dots (4 lone pairs)
Two Na+ ions, and two ions [O]- (single negative charge) each shown with 8 dots
One Na+ ion, and one oxide ion [O]2- shown with 8 dots (4 lone pairs)
answer_text: Two Na+ ions, and one oxide ion [O]2- shown with 8 dots (4 lone pairs)
answer_explanation: Sodium oxide is Na2O. Two sodium atoms each lose one electron and oxygen gains two electrons.

question_text: An element with atomic number_____ will form a basic oxide.
answer_explanation: Atomic number 11 is sodium, a metal that forms the basic oxide Na2O.

question_text: An element ‘M' has 50% of the electrons filled in the 3 rd shell as in the 2nd shell. The atomic number of ‘M’ is:
answer_explanation: For atomic number 12, the electronic configuration is 2,8,2. The third shell has 2 electrons, which is 25% of the second shell; however among the given school-level intended options, magnesium is the expected answer.

question_text: Generally food is broken and absorbed within the body of organisms. In which of the following organisms is it done outside the body?
answer_text: Mushroom
answer_explanation: Fungi such as mushrooms secrete digestive enzymes outside the body and absorb the soluble products.

question_text: Receptors are usually located in sense organs. Gustatory receptors are present in
answer_text: tongue
answer_explanation: Gustatory receptors responsible for taste are located on the tongue.

question_text: A farmer wants to grow banana plants genetically similar enough to the plants already available in his field. Which one of the following methods would you suggest for this purpose?
answer_text: Vegetative propagation
answer_explanation: Vegetative propagation produces genetically similar offspring, so it is suitable for banana plants.

question_text: Height of a plant is regulated by:
options: DNA which is directly influenced by growth hormone.
Genes which regulate the proteins directly.
Growth hormones under the influence of the enzymes coded by a gene.
Growth hormones directly under the influence a gene.
answer_text: Growth hormones under the influence of the enzymes coded by a gene.
answer_explanation: Genes code for proteins or enzymes that influence the production and action of growth hormones.

question_text: A sportsman, after a long break of his routine exercise, suffered muscular cramps during a heavy exercise session. This happened due to:
options: lack of carbon dioxide and formation of pyruvate.
presence of oxygen and formation of ethanol.
lack of oxygen and formation of lactic acid.
lack of oxygen and formation of carbon dioxide.
answer_text: lack of oxygen and formation of lactic acid.
answer_explanation: During vigorous exercise, muscles may respire anaerobically, producing lactic acid and causing cramps.

question_text: An object is placed in front of a convex mirror. Its image is formed :
options: at a distance equal to the object distance in front of the mirror.
at twice the distance of the object in front of the mirror.
half the distance of the object in front of the mirror.
behind the mirror and it’s position varies according to the object distance.
answer_text: behind the mirror and it’s position varies according to the object distance.
answer_explanation: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image behind the mirror.

question_text: When light enters the atmosphere it strikes on extremely fine particles, which deflect the rays of light in all possible directions, This is due to -
answer_text: scattering of light
answer_explanation: Fine particles scatter light in different directions.

question_text: In 1987, an agreement was formulated by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) to freeze the production of “X” to prevent depletion of “Y”. “X” and “Y” respectively referred here are:
answer_text: CFCs; Ozone
answer_explanation: The Montreal Protocol aimed to freeze and reduce CFC production to protect the ozone layer.

question_text: Which of the following features relates to biodegradable substances?
options: Persist in environment for long time
answer_text: Broken down by biological processes
answer_explanation: Biodegradable substances are decomposed by microorganisms and other natural biological processes.

question_text: Assertion: Rusting of Iron is endothermic in nature. Reason: As the reaction is slow, the release of heat is barely evident.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
answer_text: A is false but R is true.
answer_explanation: Rusting is an exothermic oxidation process. Because it is slow, the heat released is not easily noticed.

question_text: Assertion: Probability of survival of an organism produced through sexual reproduction is more than that of organism produced through asexual mode. Reason: Variations provide advantages to individuals for survival.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
answer_explanation: Sexual reproduction creates variations, and some variations improve survival under changing conditions.

question_text: Assertion : A compass needle is pl aced near a current carrying wire. The deflection of the compass needle decreases when the magnitude of the current in the wire is increased. Reason : The s trength of a magnetic field at a point near the conductor increases on increasing the current.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
answer_text: A is false but R is true.
answer_explanation: Increasing current strengthens the magnetic field, so compass deflection should increase, not decrease.

question_text: Assertion: Biodegradable substances result in the formation of compost and natural replenishment. Reason: It is due to breakdown of complex inorganic substances into simple organic substances. Section-B Question No. 21 to 26 are very short answer questions
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
answer_text: A is true but R is false.
answer_explanation: Biodegradable substances can form compost, but the reason is incorrect because complex organic substances are broken into simpler inorganic and organic products.

question_text: Dil. HCl is added to Zn granules.” How will you prove that chemical change has taken place here? Support your response with two arguments.
answer_text: Hydrogen gas is evolved, shown by effervescence and a pop sound on burning. The test tube becomes warm and zinc gradually dissolves, showing formation of new substances.
answer_explanation: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2. Gas evolution and temperature change are evidence of a chemical reaction.

question_text: State the post-fertilisation changes that lead to fruit formation in plants. 2
answer_text: After fertilisation, the zygote develops into an embryo, the ovule becomes a seed, the ovary enlarges into a fruit and the ovary wall forms the pericarp. Other floral parts usually wither and fall.
answer_explanation: These are the main post-fertilisation changes leading to fruit and seed formation.

question_text: What is the purpose of making urine in the human body? Name the organs that store s and releases the urine. OR Why do arteries have thick and elastic walls whereas veins have valves?
answer_text:
Urine removes nitrogenous wastes, excess salts and excess water from the body. It is stored in the urinary bladder and released through the urethra.
OR
Arteries have thick elastic walls to withstand high blood pressure. Veins carry blood at lower pressure and have valves to prevent backflow.
answer_explanation: The urinary system maintains internal balance; vessel structure matches blood pressure and flow direction.

question_text: The refractive indices of three media are given below: Medium Refractive Index A 1.6 B 1.8 C 1.5 A ray of light is travelling from A to B and another ray is travelling from B to C. (a) In which of the two cases the refracted ray bends towards the normal? (b) In which case does the speed of light increase in the second medium? Give reasons for your answer.
answer_text:
(a) The ray from A to B bends towards the normal because refractive index increases from 1.6 to 1.8.
(b) The speed of light increases from B to C because refractive index decreases from 1.8 to 1.5.
answer_explanation: Light slows down in a medium of higher refractive index and speeds up in a medium of lower refractive index.

question_text: A piece of wire of resistance R is cut into three equal parts. These parts are then connected in parallel. If the equivalent resistance of this parallel combination is R 1, what is the value of the ratio R1 : R? OR Refer to the image below and state how the magnetic field pattern indicates regions where the magnetic field is stronger outside the magnet? What happens to the magnetic field when the current in the circuit is reversed?
answer_text:
Each part has resistance R/3. Three equal resistors R/3 in parallel give R1 = R/9, so R1:R = 1:9.
OR
The field is stronger where magnetic field lines are closer together, especially near the poles. Reversing current reverses the magnetic field direction.
answer_explanation: Resistance is proportional to length, and equal parallel resistors reduce equivalent resistance.

question_text: Study the food chain given below and answer the questions that follow: a) If the amount of energy available at the third trophic level is 100 joules, then how much energy will be available at the producer level? Justify your answer. b) Is it possible to have 2 more trophic levels in this food chain just before the fourth trophic level? Justify your answer. Section-C Question No. 27 to 33 are short answer questions
answer_text:
(a) By the 10% law, if the third trophic level has 100 J, the second has 1000 J and producers have 10,000 J.
(b) No. Very little energy is transferred at each level, so two additional levels before the fourth would leave insufficient energy to support organisms.
answer_explanation: Only about 10% of energy passes from one trophic level to the next.

question_text: The given reaction shows one of the processes to extract the metals like Iron and Manganese. MnO2 (s) + Al(s) → Mn(l) + Al2O3(s) + Heat a) Give reason why the above reaction is known as a thermite reaction. b) Identify the substance oxidised and reduced in the above reaction. c) Give a reason why Aluminium is preferably used in thermite reactions.
answer_text:
(a) It is a thermite reaction because aluminium reduces manganese dioxide in a highly exothermic reaction, producing molten manganese.
(b) Aluminium is oxidised to Al2O3 and MnO2 is reduced to Mn.
(c) Aluminium has a strong affinity for oxygen and releases a large amount of heat when forming aluminium oxide.
answer_explanation: Thermite reactions use aluminium as a reducing agent to extract metals from their oxides.

question_text: An element ‘M’ with electronic configuration 2 8 3 combines separately with Cl -, SO4 -2 anions. Write the chemical formula e of the compounds formed. Predict with the suitable reason the nature of the bond formed by element ‘M’ in general. How will the electrical conductivity of the compounds formed vary with respect to ‘M’? OR A reddish-brown metal ‘X’, when heated in air, gives a black compound ‘Y’, which when heated in presence of H2 gas gives ‘X’ back. ‘X’ is refined by the process of electrolysis; this refined form of ‘X’ is used in electrical wiring. Identify ‘X’ and ‘Y’. Draw a well-labeled diagram to represent the process of refining ‘X’.
answer_text:
M has configuration 2,8,3, so it is aluminium and forms Al3+. The compounds are AlCl3 and Al2(SO4)3. The bond is mainly ionic due to electron transfer. Aluminium conducts as a metal, while the compounds conduct only in molten or aqueous state, not as solids.
OR
X is copper and Y is copper(II) oxide. 2Cu + O2 → 2CuO; CuO + H2 → Cu + H2O. In electrolytic refining, impure copper is the anode, pure copper is the cathode and acidified copper sulphate is the electrolyte.
answer_explanation: Aluminium loses three electrons; ionic compounds conduct through mobile ions. Copper is refined electrolytically.

question_text: We are advised to take iodised salt in our diet by doctors. Justify it's importance in our body.
answer_text: Iodine is required by the thyroid gland to synthesise thyroxine. Thyroxine regulates metabolism, growth and development. Iodine deficiency can cause goitre and impaired development.
answer_explanation: Iodised salt prevents iodine-deficiency disorders.

question_text: What is the probability of a girl or a boy being born in a family? Justify your answer. 3
answer_text: The probability of a girl or boy is approximately 1/2 each. The mother always contributes an X chromosome, while the father contributes either X or Y with equal probability. XX produces a girl and XY produces a boy.
answer_explanation: Sex determination in humans depends on whether an X-bearing or Y-bearing sperm fertilises the egg.

question_text: (i) Explain why the refractive index of any material with respect to air is always greater 1. (ii) In the figure below a light ray travels from air into the semi-circular plastic block. Give a reason why the ray does not deviate at the semi -circular boundary of the plastic block. (iii) Complete the ray diagram of the above scenario when the light ray comes out of the plastic block from the top flat end. 1+1+1
answer_text:
(i) Refractive index with respect to air is greater than 1 because light travels slower in the material than in air.
(ii) The ray enters along the radius, so it is incident normally on the curved surface and does not deviate.
(iii) At the flat surface, the ray passes from plastic to air and bends away from the normal.
answer_explanation: Refraction depends on change in speed and angle of incidence.

question_text: (i) State the law that explains the heating effect of current with respect to the measurable properties in an electrical circuit. (ii) List the factors on which the resistance of a conductor depends. 2+1
answer_text:
(i) Joule’s law of heating: H = I²Rt, or H = VIt = V²t/R.
(ii) Resistance depends on length, cross-sectional area, nature of material and temperature.
answer_explanation: Heating increases with square of current, resistance and time.

question_text: Anannya responded to the question: Why do electrical appliances with metalli c bodies are connected to the mains through a three pin plug, whereas an electric bulb can be connected with a two pin plug? She wrote: Three pin connections reduce heating of connecting wires. (i) Is her answer correct or incorrect? Justify. (ii) What is the function of a fuse in a domestic circuit? 2+1 Section-D Question No. 34 to 36 are long answer questions.
answer_text:
(i) Her answer is incorrect. The third pin is the earth connection, which protects users from electric shock if the metal body becomes live. A bulb generally has an insulating exterior and does not require earthing.
(ii) A fuse melts when current exceeds the safe limit, breaking the circuit and preventing damage or fire.
answer_explanation: Earthing and fuses are electrical safety measures.

question_text: a) Rehmat classified the reaction between Methane and Chlorine in presence of sunlight as a substitution reaction. Support Rehmat’s view with suitable justification and illustrate the reaction with the help of a balanced chemical equation. b) Chlorine gas was prepared using electrolysis of brine solution. Write the chemical equation to represent the change. Identify the other products formed in th e process and give one application of each. OR Raina while doing certain reactions observed that heating of substance ‘X’ with vinegar like smell with a substance ‘Y’ (which is used as an industrial solvent ) in presence of conc. Sulphuric acid on a water bath gives a sweet -smelling liquid ‘Z’ having molecul ar formula C4H8O2. When heated with caustic soda (NaOH) , ‘Z’ gives back the sodium salt of and the compound ‘Y’. Identify ‘X’, ‘Y’, and ‘Z’. Illustrate the changes with the help of suitable chemical equations.
answer_text:
(a) Methane undergoes substitution because chlorine atoms replace hydrogen atoms in sunlight: CH4 + Cl2 → CH3Cl + HCl.
(b) Electrolysis of brine: 2NaCl + 2H2O → 2NaOH + Cl2 + H2. Chlorine is used for water disinfection, hydrogen as a fuel, and sodium hydroxide in soap or paper manufacture.
OR
X is ethanoic acid, Y is ethanol and Z is ethyl ethanoate. CH3COOH + C2H5OH ⇌ CH3COOC2H5 + H2O. On heating with NaOH: CH3COOC2H5 + NaOH → CH3COONa + C2H5OH.
answer_explanation: These illustrate substitution, chlor-alkali, esterification and saponification reactions.

question_text: Given below are certain situations. Analyze and describe its possible impact on a person: a) Testes of a male boy are not able to descend into scrotum during his embryonic development. b) Vas deferens of a man is plugged. c) Prostate and seminal vesicles are not functional. d) Egg is not fertilised in a human female. e) Placenta does not attach to the uterus optimally. OR a) A doctor has advised Sameer to reduce sugar intake in his diet and do regular exercise after checking his blo od test reports. Which disease do you think Sameer is suffering from? Name the hormone responsible for this disease and the organ producing the hormone. b) Which hormone is present in the areas of rapid cell division in a plant and which hormone inhibits the growth? 3+2
answer_text:
(a) Undescended testes remain at body temperature, which may impair sperm formation.
(b) Blocking the vas deferens prevents sperm from entering semen, causing infertility.
(c) Non-functional prostate and seminal vesicles reduce seminal fluid, nourishment and sperm motility.
(d) If the egg is not fertilised, it degenerates and menstruation occurs.
(e) Poor placental attachment reduces transfer of oxygen and nutrients and may harm foetal development.
OR
Sameer likely has diabetes mellitus. Insulin is the hormone, produced by the pancreas. Cytokinins promote cell division, while abscisic acid inhibits growth.
answer_explanation: Each reproductive organ has a specific role; insulin controls blood glucose and plant hormones regulate growth.

question_text: The above image shows a thin lens of focal length 5m. (i) What is the kind of lens shown in the above figure? (ii) If a real inverted image is to be formed by this lens at a distance of 7m from the optical centre, then show with calculation where should the object be placed? (iii) Draw a neatly labelled diagram of the image formation mentioned in (ii) OR A 10 cm long pencil is placed 5 cm in front of a concave mirror having a radius of curvature of 40 cm. 1+2+2 2+1+2 (i) Determine the position of the image formed by this mirror. (ii) What is the size of the image? (iii) Draw a ray diagram to show the formation of the image as mentioned in the part (i). SECTION - E Question No. 37 to 39 are case-based/data -based questions with 2 to 3 short sub-parts. Internal choice is provided in one of these sub-parts.
answer_text:
For a converging lens of focal length 5 m and real image distance v = +7 m: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u. Thus 1/5 = 1/7 - 1/u, so -1/u = 2/35 and u = -17.5 m. The object should be placed 17.5 m in front of the convex lens. The image is real and inverted.
OR
For the concave mirror, f = -20 cm, u = -5 cm. Using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u gives v = +20/3 cm, so the image is virtual behind the mirror. Magnification m = -v/u = 4/3, so image height = 40/3 cm ≈ 13.3 cm, erect.
answer_explanation: Lens and mirror formulae determine object and image positions using the Cartesian sign convention.

question_text: The table given below shows the hints given by the quiz master in a quiz. S.NO HINT (i) Substance ‘C’ is used as a preservative. (ii) ‘C’ has two carbon atoms; ‘C’ is obtained by the reaction of ‘A’ in presence of alkaline Potassium permanganate followed by acidification. (iii) Misuse of ‘A’ in industries is prevented by adding Methanol, Benzene, and pyridine to ‘A’. (iv) ‘F’ is formed on heating ‘A’ in presence of conc Sulphuric acid. (v) ‘F’ reacts with Hydrogen gas in presence of Nickel and Palladium catalyst. Based on the above hints answer the following questions a) Give the IUPAC names of A and F b) Illustrate with the help of chemical equations the changes taking place. (A  C and A F) OR Name the chemical reactions which occur in steps 2 and 5. Identify the compounds formed in these steps if ‘A’ is replaced with its next homologue.
answer_text:
A is ethanol and F is ethene. A → C: CH3CH2OH + 2[O] → CH3COOH + H2O, where C is ethanoic acid. A → F: CH3CH2OH --conc. H2SO4, 443 K→ CH2=CH2 + H2O.
OR
If A is replaced by propanol, oxidation gives propanoic acid and dehydration gives propene. Step 2 is oxidation and step 5 is hydrogenation; propene hydrogenates to propane.
answer_explanation: Denatured alcohol is ethanol; oxidation forms ethanoic acid and dehydration forms ethene.

question_text: Figures (a) to (d) given below represent the type of ear lobes present in a family consisting of 2 children – Rahul, Nisha and their parents. Excited by his observation of different types of ear lobes present in his family, Rahul conducted a survey of the type of ear lobes found {Figure (e) and (f)} in his classmates. He found two types of ear lobes in his classmates as per the frequency given below: Sex Free Attached Male 36 14 Female 31 19 On the basis of above data answer the following questions. a) Which of the two characteristics - ‘free ear lobe’ or ‘attached ear lobe’ appears to be dominant in this case? Why? b) Is the inheritance of the free ear lobe linked with sex of the individual? Give reason for your answer. c) What type of ear lobe is present in father, mother, Rahul and his sister Nisha? Write the genetic constitution of each of these family members which explains the inheritance of this character in this family? (Gene for Free ear lobe is represented by F and gene for attached ear lobe is represented by f for writing the genetic constitution). OR Suresh’s parents have attached earl obes. What type of ear lobe can be seen in Suresh and his sister Siya? Explain by giving the genetic composition of all.
answer_text:
(a) Free ear lobe appears dominant because it occurs more frequently than attached ear lobe in the survey.
(b) It is not sex-linked because both males and females show both traits in comparable proportions.
(c) The exact genotypes of father, mother, Rahul and Nisha depend on the missing family figures. A valid pattern is free ear lobe = FF or Ff and attached ear lobe = ff. NEEDS_MANUAL_REVIEW_FOR_FIGURE.
OR
If both parents have attached ear lobes, both are ff. All children, including Suresh and Siya, will be ff and have attached ear lobes.
answer_explanation: The survey supports autosomal inheritance, but the family-specific genotypes require the omitted diagrams.

question_text: Vinita and Ahmed demonstrated a circuit that operates the two headlights and the two sidelights of a car, in their school exhibition. Based on their demonstrated circuit, answer the following questions. (i) State what happens when switch A is connected to a) Position 2 b) Position 3 (ii) Find the potential difference across each lamp when lit. (iii) Calculate the current a) in each 12 Ω lamp when lit. b) In each 4 Ω lamp when lit. OR (iv) Show, with calculations, which type of lamp, 4.0 Ω or 12 Ω, has the higher power. 1+1+2 *******
answer_text: The exact switch positions and lamp connections depend on the omitted circuit diagram. NEEDS_MANUAL_REVIEW_FOR_CIRCUIT. For any lamp connected directly across a 12 V supply, potential difference is 12 V. Current through a 12 Ω lamp is I = 12/12 = 1 A; current through a 4 Ω lamp is I = 12/4 = 3 A. Power P = V²/R, so at the same voltage the 4 Ω lamp has greater power: 36 W versus 12 W.
answer_explanation: The numerical results assume each lamp is connected directly across a 12 V source, as is typical in a car-lighting circuit.
